newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate rises again, baht down late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate rises again, baht down late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank continued to rise to 12.75-13.00 percent late on Friday from 11.00-12.00 percent early and 9.50-10.00 late on Thursday on a scarcity of funds in the system, dealers said.
Dealers said the liquidity was squeezed as a result of recent heavy dollar buying and the value added tax payment.
The value added tax has to be paid at the middle of every month.
Dealers said the coming reserve requirement, due next week, also made commercial banks reluctant to lend funds in the market.
"Most major local banks and some state banks lent only a small amount of funds today," said one dealer at a local bank.
The baht fell to 25.488-25.493 to the dollar late from 25.482-25.285 in early trade on the dollar's strength abroad, dealers said.
"But buying of the U.S. unit was quite thin today because baht supply was very tight and short-term baht interest rates are high," one dealer said.
The one-month dollar/baht swap premium rose to 9.00/10.00 satangs per dollar from 8.50/9.50 early on tighter liquidity, dealers said.
The mid-rate was fixed by the Bank of Thailand unchanged at 25.47.
